title: Not waking up but still breathing — roll them on their side
applies_to: Someone who does not answer you at all, but whose chest is rising and falling normally.

citations.source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: Basic Life Support
citations.section: The unresponsive person who is breathing normally

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020
citations.section: Unresponsive and breathing normally, recovery position

steps.text: Tap their shoulders and shout. If they do not answer or move, they are unresponsive.
Tilt their head back gently and lift their chin. Watch the chest and listen at the mouth for up to 10 seconds.
If the chest is rising and falling normally, call for an ambulance now and say the person is not waking up.
Roll them onto their side, facing you.
Tilt their head so the mouth points slightly down. Anything in the mouth can then drain out instead of going into the chest.
Bend the top leg and the top arm to stop them rolling onto their face.
Stay with them. Keep checking that the chest is still rising and falling normally until help arrives.
Loosen tight clothing at the neck and cover them so they stay warm.

do_not: Do not leave them lying flat on their back. If they are sick, they can choke on it.
Do not give them anything to eat or drink, and do not try to give medicine.
Do not shake them hard or slap them to wake them up.
Do not move them at all if they fell from a height or you think the neck or back is hurt, unless they are choking or being sick.
escalate_if: The chest stops rising and falling normally — roll them onto their back and start pushing on the chest.
They are bleeding heavily as well — press hard on the wound while they lie on their side.
They start shaking or jerking — do not hold them down, move hard things away, and wait for it to stop.
